standard: Field Assembly Record Standard 1.2, §8 market records; see PROVENANCE.md
notes: Signed by the editor 2026-11-16 after reading the reviewed draft. Numbers computed from run 2026-11-17T015818Z by the routine, after tools/run.py gained RUN.<title>.not_published (commit c2b7dea, 2026-11-16): the BLS API returned October 2026 for WPU0223, WPUFD4111 and both CPI-U series and no 2026 M10 row for WPU02230503 (latest flag on M09, no message, no footnote), so the gate, which waits for the lead index, would never have opened. The lobster index is carried at September 2026, the reading Issue 1 printed (198.779 in both files, still marked preliminary), and numbers.json records the absent month as ppi_lobsters_not_published. Nothing is substituted for it. Why BLS did not return the month is not known to this record; the issue says so and says BLS may publish it later. Prose drafted 2026-11-16 by a session from numbers.md and numbers.json, modeled on Issue 1; tools/check.py passes. Comparisons that do not exist: BLS marks 2025-10 '-' with 'Data unavailable due to the 2025 lapse in appropriations' for CUUR0000SEFV and CUUR0000SAF11, so neither CPI row has a year-earlier value; the record holds no 2024-09 import reading, so neither import measure has a two-year comparison. Independent review 2026-11-16 (a separate pass, read-only): recalculated from this run's captures, not numbers.json, all five BLS series with their year and two-year changes and the March peaks, the NOAA Portland September volume, unit value and year-to-date totals, the DMR September prices and the 2016 and 2025 annual landings and prices (from the PDF text), the ERS attributes, and every retail count and range from observations.jsonl; all matched. All 11 evidence.json hashes verified; the DMR PDF is byte-identical to Issue 1's. No flags for either November observation run. Applied from the review: the two revised-September-seafood figures removed and the sentence made qualitative (542.104 in this run against 543.607 in run 2026-10-18T144903Z; neither is in this computed set and the earlier capture is not in evidence.json); the September lobster reading named as preliminary; statements about a BLS 'release' reworded to what the capture is, the public API response; the out-of-stock listings inside the 152 series stated (17 on 2026-11-01: G 15, D 1, E 1; 15 on 2026-11-15, all G); the 2026 landings sentence and the March-peak sentence narrowed; the retrieval line no longer says all sources were retrieved the same evening. Open points for the editor. (1) Issue 1 printed the September seafood index as 543.6 and +20.1%; on this run's file it is 542.1, which would print +19.8%. Whether Issue 1 gets a source-revision note, as chicken and egg-butter did, is the editor's call. (2) The next-issue line carries no date because no retained capture holds the BLS release date for November PPI. (3) If BLS later returns October for WPU02230503, the declaration in config.json goes inert on its own; whether this issue then gets a note is the editor's call. Bare counts and worded quantities the gate does not read were checked by the review against the captures and the computed set: two gaps, three measures, two sellers, four of eight, 17, one, three, two, 15 of 17, nine months, four months, two weeks, 334 against 315, 'more than half' (77 of 152), 'more than a year old'.
